domain.name: Photo & Video Production
domain.description: Practical post-production knowledge for still-photo selection, Lightroom/Camera Raw, Photoshop, retouching, compositing, audio post, multicam, motion graphics, and delivery.

competencies.name: Photo Culling & Selection
competencies.description: Select the strongest images efficiently while preserving story, variety, technical quality, and client priorities.
competencies.purpose: Reduce large shoots to a coherent, high-value final set without wasting edit time on weak frames.

units.title: Three-pass culling workflow
units.content: Pass 1 removes obvious technical failures, accidental frames, duplicates, and closed-eye misses. Pass 2 compares near-duplicates for expression, timing, gesture, focus, and composition. Pass 3 checks the whole gallery for story coverage, people coverage, variety, transitions, and client must-haves before editing begins.

units.title: Select for the set, not only the single frame
units.content: The strongest isolated image is not always the best gallery choice. Favor a final set with useful variety in shot size, expression, moments, people, and sequence while protecting genuinely exceptional frames.

units.title: Culling failures
units.content: Avoid editing every usable frame, keeping five nearly identical images, deleting all imperfect-but-emotionally-important moments, overvaluing sharpness while ignoring expression, and losing key people or event milestones from the final set.

drills.title: Cull a large event set
drills.prompt: Design a culling plan for 900 event photos that must become a strong 250-photo gallery. Explain pass criteria, duplicate handling, must-have coverage, and when an imperfect frame should survive.

competencies.name: Lightroom & Camera Raw Workflow
competencies.description: Develop RAW still images efficiently with exposure, white balance, tone, color, masking, synchronization, and non-destructive organization.
competencies.purpose: Create consistent batches quickly while preserving RAW flexibility and edit traceability.

units.title: RAW development order
units.content: Confirm profile and lens corrections; set white balance; establish exposure and tonal range; shape contrast; control highlights and shadows; set color and skin carefully; apply local masks where needed; manage noise and sharpening; then synchronize only settings that are truly shared across similar frames.

units.title: Sync conditions, not assumptions
units.content: Batch syncing is powerful when lighting, camera, and scene are stable. Break synchronization when angle, flash distance, mixed light, skin exposure, or background brightness changes materially.

units.title: RAW workflow failures
units.content: Avoid copying one white balance across mixed-light scenes, using global exposure to solve local face problems, over-recovering highlights until images look flat, sharpening noisy shadows aggressively, and exporting before checking crop and masks at full resolution.

drills.title: Batch a mixed reception
drills.prompt: Plan a Lightroom or Camera Raw workflow for 120 reception photos across flash-lit tables, dance-floor LEDs, and ambient portraits. Explain where synchronization should split.

competencies.name: Photoshop Retouching
competencies.description: Perform controlled pixel-level cleanup, repair, reshaping, object removal, and finishing without making images look artificial.
competencies.purpose: Solve problems that RAW development cannot while protecting texture, anatomy, and visual credibility.

units.title: Retouching layer strategy
units.content: Work non-destructively with duplicated or empty layers where possible. Separate cleanup, tonal work, color work, and sharpening. Zoom out frequently to judge realism, and keep the original available for comparison.

units.title: Remove distractions before changing people
units.content: Fix sensor spots, background clutter, temporary blemishes, lint, and stray objects before reshaping faces or bodies. Preserve permanent features unless the job specifically calls for a different treatment.

units.title: Retouching failures
units.content: Avoid plastic skin, repeated clone patterns, bent architecture from careless transforms, haloed object removal, distorted hands or limbs, over-white teeth and eyes, and destructive edits with no path back.

drills.title: Plan a natural portrait retouch
drills.prompt: Describe a layer-by-layer Photoshop retouch for a close portrait with lint, temporary blemishes, flyaway hairs, uneven background tone, and mild under-eye darkness.

competencies.name: Natural Skin Retouching
competencies.description: Balance temporary blemish cleanup, texture preservation, tone, color, and flattering light without erasing real skin.
competencies.purpose: Deliver polished portraits that still look like the person photographed.

units.title: Texture, tone, and color are different problems
units.content: Skin texture, luminosity variation, and color variation should be evaluated separately. Blurring texture to fix tonal unevenness creates artificial skin; global saturation changes rarely solve localized redness or cast issues cleanly.

units.title: Natural skin workflow
units.content: Remove temporary distractions conservatively; correct local color casts; smooth only distracting tonal transitions using dodge/burn or restrained frequency separation; preserve pores and natural detail; then review at normal viewing size before sharpening.

units.title: Skin-retouching failures
units.content: Avoid blurring the whole face, flattening all facial shape, whitening skin, removing permanent marks without direction, making eyes unnaturally bright, and judging only at 200 percent zoom.

drills.title: Retouch without plastic skin
drills.prompt: Explain how you would retouch uneven cheek tone and temporary blemishes while preserving pores, face shape, and natural complexion.

competencies.name: Masking & Compositing
competencies.description: Combine image elements convincingly using accurate masks, matched perspective, light, color, edge quality, and depth cues.
competencies.purpose: Create believable composites and repairs that survive normal viewing and delivery resolution.

units.title: Composite matching workflow
units.content: Match perspective and scale first; refine subject mask and hair edges; match exposure and white balance; match contrast, saturation, and black level; reproduce light direction and softness; add contact shadow and environmental color spill; then match grain, sharpness, and depth-of-field.

units.title: Edges reveal the fake first
units.content: Before adding cinematic effects, inspect hair, hands, translucent fabric, reflected light, contact points, and hard-to-soft edge transitions. Small edge errors break realism faster than many global color differences.

units.title: Composite failures
units.content: Avoid perfect cutout edges in soft-focus scenes, mismatched shadow direction, different noise structure, wrong focal-plane sharpness, missing contact shadows, impossible perspective, and color spill that does not match the environment.

drills.title: Replace a portrait background
drills.prompt: Plan a believable background replacement for a full-body portrait with loose hair and floor contact. Include mask, perspective, light, shadow, color spill, and grain matching.

competencies.name: Photo Noise Reduction & Sharpening
competencies.description: Balance noise reduction, detail preservation, capture sharpening, creative sharpening, and output sharpening.
competencies.purpose: Improve clarity without producing waxy texture, halos, crunchy edges, or amplified noise.

units.title: Noise reduction and sharpening interact
units.content: Noise reduction removes high-frequency variation while sharpening increases local contrast. Strong sharpening after aggressive denoise can create false texture; sharpening noisy files before denoise can exaggerate artifacts.

units.title: Detail finishing workflow
units.content: Assess noise at representative zoom; reduce color noise first where needed; apply restrained luminance reduction; mask sharpening away from smooth areas; sharpen meaningful edges and texture; then apply output sharpening appropriate to final size and medium.

units.title: Detail-processing failures
units.content: Avoid zero-noise targets, oversharpened eyelashes and pores, halos on contrast edges, sharpening backgrounds that should remain soft, and applying the same settings to high-ISO and low-ISO files.

drills.title: Finish a high-ISO event portrait
drills.prompt: Describe a denoise and sharpening strategy for a high-ISO event portrait where skin texture matters but the background is noisy and out of focus.
rubric: Treats color and luminance noise appropriately

competencies.name: Multicam Editing
competencies.description: Synchronize and cut multi-camera footage while preserving continuity, performance timing, audio quality, and useful coverage.
competencies.purpose: Turn multiple camera angles into a coherent edit without losing the strongest performance or event moment.

units.title: Multicam setup and cut workflow
units.content: Verify frame rates and timebase; synchronize with timecode, waveform, or clear sync points; choose and lock the primary audio source; build the multicam sequence; cut first for content and performance; then smooth visual continuity and remove angle changes that do not add value.

units.title: Audio continuity is the spine
units.content: A multicam edit can survive imperfect visual continuity more easily than broken dialogue or performance timing. Stabilize and protect the primary audio timeline before chasing camera changes.

units.title: Multicam failures
units.content: Avoid drifting sync, switching angles on every beat, cutting to an angle with worse performance just for variety, mixing mismatched audio sources mid-sentence, and leaving camera color/exposure differences untreated.

drills.title: Cut a ceremony multicam
drills.prompt: Plan a multicam workflow for three cameras plus a recorder at a ceremony. Explain sync, primary audio, angle priorities, and how you would handle a camera that briefly stops recording.

competencies.name: Audio Post-Production
competencies.description: Edit dialogue, music, ambience, noise, dynamics, and loudness for clean, intelligible finished video.
competencies.purpose: Make audio feel controlled, consistent, and intentional across speakers, scenes, and delivery platforms.

units.title: Dialogue-first mix workflow
units.content: Organize tracks; repair obvious clicks and gaps; reduce noise conservatively; shape dialogue with EQ; control peaks with compression or automation; build ambience and music around intelligibility; use meters for peak and loudness checks; then listen on headphones and ordinary speakers.

units.title: Fix with editing before heavy processing
units.content: Clip gain, fades, room tone, alternate takes, and selective repair often sound more natural than aggressive broadband denoise or extreme compression applied to the entire track.

units.title: Audio-post failures
units.content: Avoid pumping denoise, clipped exports, inconsistent speaker level, music masking dialogue, hard cuts in room tone, excessive low-end rumble, and loudness decisions made on one playback device only.

drills.title: Clean an interview mix
drills.prompt: Plan an audio-post chain for an interview with HVAC rumble, occasional clothing noise, uneven speaking level, and background music.

competencies.name: Motion Graphics & Titles
competencies.description: Create readable, branded, well-timed lower thirds, titles, callouts, and simple motion systems.
competencies.purpose: Add information and brand polish without distracting from the content.

units.title: Title-system workflow
units.content: Define hierarchy and safe margins; select a small type system; build reusable alignment rules; animate with clear entrance, hold, and exit timing; check readability over moving footage; test at actual delivery size; then package reusable templates where possible.

units.title: Motion should explain hierarchy
units.content: Use animation to guide attention or reveal information order. Movement that does not support hierarchy, brand, rhythm, or comprehension is usually decoration and should be reduced.

units.title: Motion-graphics failures
units.content: Avoid tiny type, excessive easing tricks, every element moving differently, low-contrast text over footage, inconsistent padding, long animations that slow the edit, and brand systems that change from title to title.

drills.title: Design a lower-third system
drills.prompt: Design a reusable lower-third system for interviews that includes name, role, long-name handling, safe margins, animation timing, and readability over varied footage.

competencies.name: Export, Codecs & Delivery
competencies.description: Choose mezzanine, delivery, archival, and platform export settings based on quality, editability, file size, color, and playback requirements.
competencies.purpose: Deliver files that look correct, play reliably, and remain useful for future revisions.

units.title: Codec choice follows the job
units.content: Editing intermediates prioritize quality and decode performance; delivery codecs prioritize size and compatibility; archival masters prioritize recoverable quality and future use. One export format should not automatically serve every purpose.

units.title: Delivery QC workflow
units.content: Confirm resolution, frame rate, color space, audio channels, duration, filename/version, and target codec; export; watch beginning, middle, and end plus high-motion and dark scenes; check audio; inspect captions if present; verify file playback outside the editor; then preserve a high-quality master when warranted.

units.title: Export failures
units.content: Avoid wrong frame rate, accidental variable scaling, clipped audio, crushed levels from color-range mistakes, duplicate generation loss from repeated transcodes, ambiguous filenames, and delivering only the compressed social copy with no master.

drills.title: Build a delivery matrix
drills.prompt: Create an export plan for a 4K event film that needs a high-quality master, YouTube upload, vertical social clips, and future revision capability.
